import re
import sys
from datetime import date

RELEASE_NOTES_FILE = "docs/en/docs/release-notes.md"
RELEASE_HEADER_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^## (\d+\.\d+\.\d+)\s*(\(.*\))?\s*$")


def main() -> None:
    with open(RELEASE_NOTES_FILE) as f:
        lines = f.readlines()

    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        match = RELEASE_HEADER_PATTERN.match(line)
        if not match:
            continue

        version = match.group(1)
        date_part = match.group(2)

        if date_part:
            print(f"Latest release {version} already has a date: {date_part}")
            sys.exit(0)

        today = date.today().isoformat()
        lines[i] = f"## {version} ({today})\n"
        print(f"Added date: {version} ({today})")

        with open(RELEASE_NOTES_FILE, "w") as f:
            f.writelines(lines)
        sys.exit(0)

    print("No release header found")
    sys.exit(1)

    release_notes_file = Path("docs/en/docs/release-notes.md")
    content = release_notes_file.read_text()
    
    # Check if the version header already exists
    if f"## {version}" in content:
        print(f"Version header ## {version} already exists in {release_notes_file}")
        return

    # Insert the version header after "## Latest Changes"
    # We want to insert it before the first versioned header if "## Latest Changes" is not found,
    # but usually "## Latest Changes" is at the top.
    
    if "## Latest Changes" in content:

        # The "## Latest Changes" section ends when the next "## " header starts.

                else:

            release_notes_file.write_text(new_content)
            print(f"Added version header ## {version} to {release_notes_file}")
        else:
            # No versioned header found, just append to the end
            release_notes_file.write_text(content + f"\n\n## {version}\n")
            print(f"Added version header ## {version} to the end of {release_notes_file}")
